newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. condemns Milosevic over poll abuse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns Milosevic over poll abuse.

text.p: The United States on Monday strongly condemned Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic for annulling opposition victories in local elections and threatened him with international isolation unless he backed down.

"Today, we join in condemning the Serbian government decision to ignore the results of the November 17 election. That decision must be reversed," U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said at the start of a two-day meeting of NATO foreign ministers.
Christopher said the people of Serbia had the right to expect the same treatment as their central European neighbours. That, he said, meant: "Clean elections, a free press, a normal market economy."
He added that if Milosevic accepted the democratic will his country could enjoy the "legitimacy and assistance it needs", but warned:
"If he seeks to rule Serbia as an unreformed dictatorship it will only increase his isolation and the suffering of his people."
It was the clearest hint yet that Washington would back the reimposition of sanctions on Serbia unless Milosevic accepted the results of the November polls.
